FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Raw materials for Paints, Varnishes and Related Product Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Chemical Division Council. 


This Indian Standard originally was published in 1981 by bifurcating IS 411 : 1968. Titanium dioxide is one of 
the most important pigments used in paint industry. The material is mainly of two types, namely, anatase and 
rutile and both are used substantially in paint industry. Though both types of pigment are chemically similar, they 
differ in crystalline structure and hence in physical properties. The type is identified more accurately by X-ray 
diffraction than the relative density. In this standard rutile grade is covered and anatase grade is covered under 
IS 411. 


The titanium dioxide, rutile, manufactured by chloride or sulphate process, has been classified in three grades so 
as to suit the different end uses of the pigment in paint industry. The modern rutile pigment is characterized by 
the type, amount, and manner of deposition of surface treatment compounds. The manufacturers may indicate the 
type of inorganic and organic treatment given to allow for this, and for convenience, the grades are classified 
according to titanium dioxide content. 


This revision has been taken to bring out the standard in the latest style and format of the Indian Standard. It also 
incorporates amendments issued to the last version of the standard. In addition, the following changes have been 
made: 


a) The zinc reduction method has been replaced by UV-Vis-spectrophotometer for titanium dioxide content 
determination; 

b) The conductivity bridge method for determination resistivity of aqueous extract has been replaced with 
updated test method; 

c) Lead and toxic heavy metals restriction have been prescribed; 

d) Various editorial corrections have been made; and 

e) References have been updated. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex L. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 2022. The 
number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in 
this standard. 


IS 9788 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


TITANIUM DIOXIDE, RUTILE FOR PAINTS — 
SPECIFICATION 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes requirements and methods 
of sampling and test for rutile titanium dioxide used 
as a pigment in paint industry. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent editions of these standards. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, definitions of terms 
(including approved sample) given in IS 1303 and 
under 2 of IS 33 and following shall be apply. 


3.1 Registered Sample — Sample supplied in 
advance by a prospective supplier and registered by 
the approved testing authorities after testing it to all 
the requirements of this standard. A complete record 
of its performance shall be kept in respect of all tests. 


3.2 Approved Sample — The sample accepted by 
the indentor or inspection authority as the basis for 
supply. When a sample is tested and approved by the 
purchaser or inspection authority, the result of such 
tests as permits the supplier to meet the limits 
imposed by the specification for deliveries shall be 
made available to the supplier. 


4 GRADES 


4.1 The material shall be of the following three 
grades depending on surface treatment and titanium 
dioxide (percent rutile) content: 


a) Grade Ri; 
b) Grade R2; and 
c) Grade R3, 


4.1.1 The manufacturers shall declare the modifiers 
used for surface treatment of rutile titanium dioxide. 


5 REQUIREMENTS 
5.1 Description 


The material shall be a soft, dry powder and shall 
consist essentially of titanium dioxide of rutile 
crystalline structure as determined by XRD (X-ray 
Diffraction) method prescribed in Annex A of 
IS 411. 


5.2 Composition 


The material after drying to a constant mass at 
100 °C + 2 °C, when determined as prescribed in 
Annex B, shall contain titanium dioxide as specified 
in Table 1. 


5.2.1 The rutile content shall be 99 percent, Min, of 
the titanium dioxide content as determined by XRD 
method prescribed in Annex A of IS 411. 


5.3 Resistance to Chalking 


When tested as prescribed in Annex C, the time 
taken for the commencement of chalking in a paint 
film incorporating the material shall be not less than 
that of a paint film incorporating the approved 
sample prepared and tested in the same manner, at 
the same time and by the same person. 


5.4 Dispersibility 


The material when tested as prescribed in Annex D 
shall pass the test and shall be not inferior (in 
reverting of finish or re-agglomeration) to that of the 
approved sample. 


5.5 Durability 


The material, when tested as prescribed in Annex E, 
shall pass the test. 


5.6 Lead Restriction 


The material shall be tested for restriction from lead 
in accordance with IS 101 (Part 8/Sec 5). When thus 
tested the material shall not contain lead or 
compounds of lead or mixtures of both, calculated 
as metallic lead exceeding 90 ppm (see NOTE). 


IS 9788 : 2023 


NOTE — When no lead is used during production, the 
product is considered lead free. 


5.7 Toxic Heavy Metal Restriction 


Product shall not be manufactured using mercury 
and mercury compounds, cadmium, chromium VI, 
arsenic, antimony, and their oxides. The material 
shall not contain more than 0.1 percent by weight in 
total of above toxic heavy metals in the form of 
natural impurities or impurities entailed by the 
production process which are contained in the raw 
material when tested by the relevant atomic 
absorption spectroscopic methods. 

NOTE —The test method procedure of AAS method is 


under preparation, till that this requirement may keep under 
abeyance. 


5.8 Special Properties 


The material shall have ease of dispersion, gloss and 
gloss retention and opacity similar to those of the 
approved sample of paint prepared as given in 
E-1.2 and when tested as prescribed in IS 101 
(Part 3/Sec 5), IS 101 (Part 4/Sec 4) and IS 101 
(Part 4/Sec 1), respectively. 


5.9 The material shall also comply with the 
requirements given in Table 1. 


6 PACKING AND MARKING 
6.1 Packing 


Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser 
and the supplier, the material shall be suitably 
packed in multiply paper bags. 


6.2 Marking 


The packing shall be securely closed and marked 
with the following particulars: 


a) Name of the material; 
b) Manufacturer's name and trade-mark, if any; 
c) Mass of the material; 
d) Lead content (Max); 
e) Toxic heavy metals content; 
f) Batch number or lot number in code or 
otherwise; 
g) Month and year of manufacture; and 
h) A cautionary note as below: 
1) Keep out of reach of children; or 
2) This product may be harmful 


if swallowed or inhaled. 


NOTE — However, it may be within 
+ 10 percent of the approved sample, if any.

ANNEX B 
[Clause 5.2 and Table 1, SI No. oO 
DETERMINATION OF TITANIUM DIOXIDE CONTENT 


B-0 GENERAL 


Two methods for determination of titanium dioxide 
have been prescribed. For routine testing, either 
Method 1 or Method 2 may be followed, but in case 
of dispute, Method 1 shall be followed. 


B-1 METHOD 1: UV-VIS 
SPECTROPHOTOMETER 


B-1.0 Outline of Method 


In this test, titanium dioxide is acid extracted by 
digesting with concentrated sulphuric acid. The acid 
extract is then diluted and treated with hydrogen 
peroxide to form a peroxo complex of titanium. 
Titanium dioxide is then photometrically estimated 
using UV-Vis spectrophotometer. 


B-1.1 Reagents 


B-1.1.1 Concentrated Sulphuric Acid — 98 percent 
AR grade (see IS 266) 


B-1.1.2 Hydrogen Peroxide — 30 percent AR grade 
B-1.1.3 Ammonium Sulphate 

B-1.1.4 Sulphuric Acid — 1 : 1 water (v/v) mixture 
B-1.2 Procedure 


Take about 5 g of the sample and dry it in the open 
weighing bottle at 105 °C + 2 °C to constant mass. 
Cap the bottle and allow it to cool to room 
temperature in the desiccator. Weigh out, to the 
nearest 0.1 mg, 0.2 gm of this test sample in to a 
500 ml glass beaker and add 25 ml of concentrated 
sulphuric acid followed by 20 g ammonium 
sulphate. Cover the beaker with a watch glass and 
heat it over a pre heated hot plate until a clear 
yellowish solution is obtained. Intermittently mix 
the contents well using glass rod. This process will 
take around 60 min to 90 min. Cool the contents and 
dilute it carefully with about 150 ml of distilled 
water. Transfer the contents into a 250 ml 
volumetric flask. Give sufficient washings to the 
beaker and every time transfer the washings into the 
volumetric flask. Make up to the volume with water 
and mix the contents well. Filter the solution through 
Whatman filter paper no 541. Label this as solution 
A. Pipette out 5 ml of solution A into a 50 ml 


volumetric flask and dilute it to mark with distilled 
water. Label this as solution B. Pipette out 10 ml of 
solution B in a 50 ml volumetric flask and add 5 ml 
of 1 : 1 sulphuric acid-water mixture followed by 
2.5 ml of hydrogen peroxide and make it up to the 
mark with distilled water. Measure the absorbance 
of the yellow-colored complex at 410 nm. 
Determine the concentration of "DO: (C) using 
calibration curve prepared from standard solutions 
of analytical reagent grade of titanium dioxide 
(see B-1.3). Estimate the titanium dioxide content 
using: 


Weg ees : 2.085 42 xC 
Percent of titanium dioxide (TiO) = —————— 


where 


C = concentration, in ppm, obtained from 
calibrate graph; and 


w = mass of TiOd, in g. 


B-1.3 Preparation of Standard "DO: for 
Calibration Curve 


B-1.3.1 Weigh accurately 0.417 0 gm of AR grade 
or high purity (© 99.5 %) grade TO: in 250 ml 
beaker and add 20 g of ammonium sulfate and 25 ml 
of concentrated sulphuric acid. 


B-1.3.2 Place the mixture on a hot plate preheated to 
245 °C + 5 °C. Continue the heating for about 
45 min to 90 min till the solution becomes clear. 


B-1.3.3 Cut off the heating, take out the beaker and 
cool the solution for 10 min to 12 min and dilute 
carefully to 1 000 ml with distilled water in a 1 litre 
volumetric flask. This corresponds to 250 ppm of 
titanium stock solution (I). Keep it aside for 30 min 
for maturation. 


B-1.3.4 Pipette out 25 ml of this stock solution (I) 
and dilute to 250 ml. This gives 25 ppm titanium 
stock solution (II). 


B-1.3.5 From titanium stock solution (ID) prepare of 
5.0 ppm, 7.5 ppm, 10.0 ppm, 15.0 ppm and 
20.0 ppm of titanium (IV) complex solutions by 
adding 1 : 1 sulphuric acid and hydrogen peroxide 
as indicated in the Table 2.

iv) 15 30 5 25 
v) 20 40 5 2.5 


Measure the absorbance of the yellow-colored 
complex after 10 min at 410 nm. Use distilled water 
as reference. Record the data and make a 
calibration curve by using spectrophotometer 
software or in microsoft excel. Plot absorbance in 
Y axis and concentration in X axis. Fit the points 
using linear equation (y = mx). 


B-2 METHOD 2: ALUMINIUM REDUCTION 
METHOD 


B-2.0 Outline of the Method 


This method is similar to zinc reduction method, but 
easier and quicker to operate. Titanium is reduced to 
trivalent state by aluminium and titrated against 
ferric ammonium sulphate using ammonium 
thiocyanate as indicator. 


B-2.1 Apparatus 


B-2.1.1 Delivery Tube — made of 4 mm internal 
diameter glass tube bent in such a way as to have a 
horizontal run of about 150 mm and vertical drop of 
about 75 mm at one end, and a vertical drop of about 
150 mm at the other end. 


B-2.1.2 Long Necked Flask — 500 ml capacity 
B-2.2 Reagents 
B-2.2.1 Ammonium Sulphate — (see IS 826) 


B-2.2.2 Sulphuric Acid — relative density 1.84 
(see IS 266) 


B-2.2.3 Hydrochloric Acid — relative density 1.19 
(see IS 265) 


B-2.2.4 Aluminium Foil — electrolytic grade 
B-2.2.5 Sodium Bicarbonate Solution — saturated 
B-2.2.6 Ammonium Thiocyanate Indicator Solution 


Prepare by dissolving 24.5 g of ammonium 
thiocyanate in 80 ml of hot water, filter and cool to 
room temperature, dilute to 100 ml and preserve in 
a well stoppered amber coloured bottle. 


B-2.2.7 Standard Ferric Ammonium Sulphate 
Solution 


Prepare by dissolving 30.16 g of fresh ferric 
ammonium sulphate in 800 ml of water containing 
15 ml of concentrated sulphric acid (see IS 266). 
Add 0.1 N potassium permanganate solution until a 
very slight pink colour is obtained. Dilute to 
1 000 ml and mix thoroughly. Filter if necessary. 
Standardize with 0.190 g to 0.210 g of standard 
titanium dioxide as prescribed in B-2.3 and calculate 
titanium dioxide equivalent of solution in g of 
titanium dioxide per ml of solution as given below: 


Mx P 


Titani S E 
itanium dioxide equivalen V x100 


where 


M = mass, in g, of standard titanium dioxide 
(T102) taken for test; 


P = percent of TiO: in standard titanium dioxide 
used; and 


V = volume, in ml, of ferric ammonium sulphate 
solution required for titration. 


B-2.3 Procedure 


B-2.3.1 Weigh accurately 0.190 g to 0.210 g of dry 
material and transfer the same to a 500 ml long 
necked flask Add 7 g to 9 g of ammonium sulphate 
and 20 ml of sulphuric acid. Mix carefully. Heat on 
a hot plate to fuming and over a strong flame until 
dissolution is complete. Cool and add 120 ml of 
water and 20 ml of hydrochloric acid. Boil the 
contents and remove from heat. 


B-2.3.2 Insert the short end of the delivery tube into 
one hole of a two hole rubber stopper suitable for the 
long necked flask. Insert a glass rod with a hook at 
the bottom end in the other hole in such a way that 
the bottom end shall be nearer to the bottom of the 
flask when the stopper is fitted into the flask. Attach 
1 g of aluminium foil to the bottom end of the rod 
by coiling it around the rod. Insert the stopper 
carrying the rod with foil and delivery tube into the 
flask in such a way that the foil is near the bottom of 
the flask and at the same time the long end of the 
delivery tube is near the bottom of a 250 ml beaker 
containing 150 ml of sodium bicarbonate solution. 


B-2.3.3 Heat the flask as soon as the dissolution of 
aluminium is completed to gentle boiling for 3 min 


IS 9788 : 2023 


to 5 min without disturbing the assembly. Cool to 
60 °C by partial immersion in water and siphon the 
sodium bicarbonate solution into the flask giving an 
atmosphere of carbon dioxide over the reduced 
titanium solution. Withdraw the stopper, rinse the 
glass water, catching the rinsings in the flask. Add 
2 ml of ammonium thiocyanate indicator solution 
and titrate immediately against standard ferric alum 
solution to a straw coloured end point. 


B-2.4 Calculation 


Calculate the percentage of titanium dioxide (TiO) 
as follows: 


VxEx 100 


TiO, content, percent by mass = M 
where 


V = volume, in ml, of ferric ammonium 
sulphate solution used in the test; 


E = titanium dioxide equivalent (see 
B-2.2.7) of ferric ammonium sulphate 
solution in g/ml; and 


M = mass, in g, of material taken for the test.

ANNEX C 
(Clause 5.3) 
DETERMINATION OF RESISTANCE TO CHALKING 


C-0 GENERAL 
C-0.1 Outline of the Method 


The pigment under test and the approved sample are 
converted into paints, applied to separate test panels 
and subjected to outdoor exposure. A piece of 
suitable cloth is drawn across the surface of the film 
under specific conditions and the surface examined 
for any chalking. 


C-1 PREPARATION OF THE PAINT 


Paints of the sample under test and the approved 
sample shall be prepared as given in E-1.2, E-1.3 
and E-1.4. 


C-2 PREPARATION OF THE TEST PANEL 


Apply the two paints vertically side by side on the 
same panel which shall be of wood or of any other 
material, agreed to between the purchaser and the 
supplier and give identical outside exposure at an 


angle of 45° facing south. The area of each paint 
exposed shall be not less than 120 cm?. Determine 
the time taken for chalking to commence by 
fortnightly examination of the panel by the 
procedure prescribed under B-3. 


C-3 PROCEDURE 


Draw a piece of black cloth, such as velvet, silesian, 
italian or some other suitable cloth of approximately 
25 mm x 100 mm size, under a load of 100 g applied 
through a disc of soft rubber of 25 mm diameter and 
about 32 mm thick, over the surface of the paint for 
a distance of 50 mm in approximately one second 
while the panel sets in a horizontal position. 


C-4 OBSERVATION 


Chalking shall be considered to have commenced 
when the surface of the black cloth is just 
perceptibly marked white. 


IS 9788 : 2023 


ANNEX D 
(Clause 5.4) 
DETERMINATION OF DISPERSIBILITY 


D-0 GENERAL 


D-0.1 For the determination of dispersion of 
titanium dioxide, high speed shear mill (see D-1.1) 
is used. It consists of a stainless steel cup with a 
cowles type impeller effective use of high speed 
disperser depends on establishing a satisfactory 
relationship between all the variables, the most 
important of which are the composition and volume 
of the mill base, dimensions of the impeller and the 
tank, location of the impeller within the tank and 
impeller speed. Some of these are inter-dependent 
and balance shall be worked out for each individual 
system 


D-0.2 Mill Base Formulation 


For good results, a high mill base viscosity is 
essential, but alone it is not enough. By using a 
medium of higher solids content, the pigment 
particles are not wetted properly and hence for better 
results the medium solids are kept as low as 
possible. This facilitates wetting and the required 
adhesion at the impeller mill base interface. The 
limits for medium solids are 15 percent to 40 percent 
and when this medium is used to achieve high 
viscosity, the pigmentation has to be increased. For 
good results, the pigment content shall be 42 percent 
by volume calculated on the total volume of the mill 
base (approximately equal to 75 percent by mass). 
Even while doing accurate formulation for mill base, 
there are factors like dilatancy and thixotropy, which 
keep on changing, depending on the shear rate 
operated in the tank. The shear transmission 
problems can be usually overcome by modifying the 
mill base conditions or mill base composition. The 
following are some of the measures that may be 
employed: 


a) Decrease the mill speed (this remedies only 
excessive dilatancy); 


b) Use of narrow container (alternatively use a 
larger impeller and decrease the mill speed 
proportionately); 


c) Increase the binder solids (40 percent should 
be regarded as maximum); 


d) Change the solvent composition; 


e) Change or modify the dispersion medium, 
namely, mill in an alkyd/amino mixture 
instead of alkyd resin alone; and 


f) Decrease slightly the pigment content of the 
mill base. 


D-1 APPARATUS 


D-1.1 The dimensions for tank impeller and charge 
and the rpm shall be as follows: 


When D is the diameter of impeller, the tank shall 
have 2 D to 3 D as internal diameter. The impeller 
shall be fixed at 0.5 D above the base of the tank. 
The charge to be added for better results shall have 
a depth of 1.8 D. The impeller will have 
1 050 metres per minute to 1 350 metres per minute 
as peripheral speed: 
Peripheral speed 


Rotor speed, N = D x 31.8 


D-2 MILLING TIME 
D-2.1 10 Minutes to 15 Minutes 


For satisfactory dispersion, a milling time of 10 min 
is recommended. Dispersion is said to be 
satisfactory if the required fineness is achieved in 
10 min. If satisfactory dispersion is not induced 
within 15 min, still longer milling is most unlikely 
to improve the fineness. 


D-3 PROCEDURE 


D-3.1 Weigh the calculated amount of medium at 
35 percent of non-volatile content (NVC) and the 
pigment in the container. Mix them using a spatula 
and transfer the contents to the tank. Run the 
impeller at the required speed. After 10 min check 
the fineness on a Hegman gauge. 


D-3.2 Continue milling for another 5 min and check 
the fineness on Hegman gauge. 


D-4 OBSERVATION 


Compare the fineness reading of the sample with 
that of the approved sample. 


IS 9788 : 2023 


ANNEX E 
(Clause 5.5) 
TEST FOR DURABILITY 


E-0 GENERAL 


The paint formulated as prescribed in F-1.2, F-1.3 
and F-1.4, when tested in accelerated weathering 
unit of carbon arc type for 21 days as prescribed in 
Annex C of IS 2932, shall not show chalk resistance, 
gloss retention, colour retention, checking and 
cracking inferior to that of the approved sample. 
Xenon arc type weatherometer may also be used in 
place of carbon arc type weathering unit. 


E-1 PROCEDURE 


Test the paint formulated with the material as given 


in E-0 by the accelerated weathering method 
prescribed in Annex C of IS 2932. Evaluate the 
performance of the material by the method of rating 
prescribed in Annex C of IS 2932. Treat the 
approved sample in a similar manner and subject to 
accelerated weathering tests simultaneously. The 
material shall be taken to have passed the 
requirement for durability if the performance of the 
paint prepared with the sample under test is not 
inferior to that of the paint prepared with the 
approved sample in respect of characteristics for 
gloss retention, chalk resistance, colour retention, 
checking and cracking. 


IS 9788 : 2023 


ANNEX F 
[Table 1, SI No. oul 
DETERMINATION OF MASS COLOUR 


F-0 GENERAL 


For the determination of mass colour, paints of 
sample under test and the approved sample are 
prepared. The quantification of colour values may 
be made by the use of instrument, wherever 
possible; otherwise, a drawdown may be drawn of 
the sample under test and the approved sample and 
visually compared. 


F-1 PAINT PREPARATION 
F-1.1 Requirements 


F-1.1.1 Alkyd Resin Medium — Jong semi-drying 
oil, alkyd, with pentaerythritol with oil length of 
60 percent to 65 percent 


F-1.1.2 Pigments — 30 percent by mass 


F-1.1.3 Pigment-Volume-Concentration (PVC) — 
20 percent 


F-1.1.4 Solvents — petroleum hydrocarbon solvents 
(see IS 1745) 


F-1.1.5 Driers — The following driers on metal 
content basis of the non-volatile matter in the 
medium shall be used: 


a) 0.06 percent cobalt octoate; and 
b) 0.5 percent lead octoate. 


F-1.1.6 Film Application — with applicator of 
50 um so as to give dry film thickness of 
approximately 25 um 


F-1.2 Formulation for Air-Drying Alkyd Gloss 
Paint 


F-1.2.1 The paint shall be prepared as follows. 


F-1.2.1.1 In 220 ml, glass jar take the following 
materials: 


a) 130 g of gloss ballotini; 
b) 60 g of titanium dioxide (TiO2); and 


c) 20 g of alkyd resin at 20 percent non-volatile 
component (NVC). 


F-1.2.1.2 Ball mill for (18 + 2) h. 
F-1.2.1.3 Then add 


a) 10 ml of petroleum hydrocarbon solvent, low 
aromatic (see IS 1745); 


b) 75 ml of mixed driers; 


c) 0.5 ml of methyl ethyl keto (MEK) oxime or 
equivalent anti skinning agent; and 


e) 101 g of alkyd resin at 70 percent NVC. 
OR 


F-1.2.1.4 In 1 000 ml glass jar add: 

a) 600 g of glass ballotini; 

b) 300 g of TiO2; and 

c) 100 g of alkyd resin at 20 percent NVC. 
F-1.2.1.5 Ball mill for 18 h +2 h. 
F-1.2.1.6 Then add 


a) 50 ml of petroleum hydrocarbon solvent, low 
aromatic (see IS 1745); 


b) 30 ml of mixed driers; 


c) 2 ml of methyl ethyl keto (MLK) oxime or 
equivalent anti skinning agent; and 


d) 500 g of alkyd resin at 70 percent NVC. 


F-1.2.2 Into a clean jar, weigh appropriate amounts 
of ballotini, resin solution and the pigment under test 
as described above. In another clean jar, weigh the 
identical quantities of the approved pigment. Screw 
the lids on to the jars and shake till the pigment is 
wetted. 


F-1.2.3 Place the jars on a suitable milling 
equipment (trundler) and mill its contents overnight 
(18h+2h). 


F-1.2.4 Scrap any dry pigment still adhering to the 
neck of the jar or to the lid after 30 min trundling 
into the mill base. 


F-1.2.5 After the milling, remove the jar from the 
trundler. Check the finish of the mill base on 
Hegman gauge, this should be less than 10 microns. 
Then add the medium, solvent, driers and anti- 
skinning agent. Add the calculated quantity, so that 
the paint shall have 20 percent pigment volume 
concentration. Return the jars on trundlers and mix 
the mill base thoroughly. Remove the ballotini by 
pouring the contents of the jar through a metal filter 
funnel. Collect the filtrate in a suitable can. 


IS 9788 : 2023 


F-1.3 Formulation for Exterior Emulsion Paint 
F-1.3.1 Pigment Binder Ratio — 1.86 
F-1.3.2 Milling Vessel — eleven cm high and 


8.5 cm in diameter, laboratory high speed impeller 


mill (Cowles type impeller) 


F-1.3.3 Materials — Add the following 
ingredients in the milling vessel as specified: 


SI No. Ingredient Content 
(1) (2) (3) 
i) TO 212g 
ii) Talc 79 g 
ili) Barytes 44¢ 
iv) 5 percent solution of sodium (Premixed) 
hexametaphosphate (NaPO3)6 35 parts 
v) Hydroxyl ethyl cellulose (HEC) 106 parts 
solution (see Note) 215.2g 
vi) Water 62 parts 
vii) Butyl carbitol acetate 35 parts 
viii) 10 percent ammonia 37 parts 


F-1.3.4 Mill for 5 min at 12 000 rpm. 


F-1.3.5 In one litre of the material weigh as given 
below: 


a) Vinyl acetate copolymer (56 percent non- 
volatile) 257 g; and 
b) Millbase 440 g. 


F-1.3.6 Stir by hand for 10 min for even and 
homogeneous mixing. 


NOTE — A specific percentage solution of HEC which will 
have viscosity of 50 to 60 p on Brookfield, RVT model on 
spindle No 6, 50 rev/min. 


F-1.4 Formulation of Stoving Alkyd Gloss Paint 
F-1.4.1 Ingredients 


F-1.4.1.1 Alkyd resin — short coconut oil alkyd with 
glycerol with oil length of 30 percent to 40 percent 


F-1.4.1.2 Pigment — 18 percent by mass 


F-1.4.1.3 Pigment volume concentration (PVC) — 
10 percent 


F-1.4.1.4 Pigment and binder ratio — 1.2 


F-1.4.1.5 Alkyd and melamine formaldehyde ratio 
— 4.1 


F-1.4.1.6 Solvents — xylene and butyl alcohol 


F-1.4.1.7 Additives — zinc naphthenate having 
metal content of 2 percent solution in petroleum 
hydrocarbon solvents 


F-1.4.2 Paint Preparation 
F-1.4.2.1 In 2 000 ml, porcelain pot mill, take the 


following materials: 
a) 1200 ml of pebbles; 
b) 540 g of titanium dioxide; 
c) 170 g of alkyd resin at 40 percent non- 
volatile component; and 


d) 15 g of zinc naphthenate solution. 


F-1.4.2.2 Ball mill for 36 h to less than 5 microns, 
then add the following: 


a) 60 g of xylene; 

b) 120 g of butyl alcohol; 

c) 1640 g of alkyd resin at 50 percent non- 
volatile component; 

d) 400 g of malamine formaldehyde resin at 
55 percent non-volatile component; and 

e) 5g of xylene to adjust viscosity. 


F-1.5 Preparation and Examination of Panels 


F-1.5.1 Place a white card or some other preferred 
substrate on a convenient horizontal surface. 


F-1.5.2 Transfer the paint under test to the card 
giving a pool that is adjacent to but separated from 
the pool of similarly made paint containing a 
standard pigment. Draw down the paints with a 
smooth stroke of a wire wound applicator. Place the 
panel horizontally in a ventilated drying cabinet and 
allow the paint to dry overnight. 


F-1.5.3 Visually compare the dry paint film with the 
standard paint film under approved artificial 
lightening conditions. A numerical assessment of 
colour may be made, provided a suitable colour 
meter is available. 


IS 9788 : 2023 


ANNEX G 
[Table 1, SI No. (iii)] 
DETERMINATION OF REDUCING POWER 


G-0 GENERAL 


Titanium dioxide is tinted with diluted 
phthalocyanine green pigment and the reducing 
power is determined. The reducing power is 
expressed in the same manner as in Reynold 
number. In Reynold number, ultramarine blue 
pigment is used; here it is replaced by 
phthalocyanine green and the tinting strength of the 
pigment is being designated as 'ISI Tinting Strength 
Number’. 


G-1 PROCEDURE 
G-1.1 Diluted Phthalocyanine Green Powder 


Dry phthalocyanine green pigment and blanc fixe 
separately at 105 °C for 2 h or till free of moisture. 
Take 1 g of dried powder of phthalocyanine green 


and 99 g of dried powder of blanc fixe in a suitable 
porcelain jar containing 20 mm porcelain heavy 
density balls. Grind the mixture for 24 h and then 
collect and store in a well stoppered bottle. Use the 
mixture for determination of ISI tinting strength 
number. 


G-1.2 Weigh 0 5 g of the titanium dioxide pigment 
under test and phthalocyanine green powder as per 
the chart given in Table 3. Mix on mullet with acid 
refined linseed oil conforming to IS 75 and prepare 
a paste. Draw a drawdown of sample and standard 
on a glass plate using a suitable applicator. 


G-1.3 Observation 


Observe the reducing power immediately and record 
the result. 


Table 3 Quantity of Phthalocyanine Green and Oil to be Taken for Test 


(Clause G-1.2) 


SI No. ISI Tinting Strength No. Phthalocyanine Green Oil 
Powder 

ml ml 

(1) (2) (3) (4) 
i) 1500 1 500 058 
ii) 1 600 1 600 061 
iii) 1 700 1 700 064 
iv) 1 800 1 800 067 


IS 9788 : 2023 


ANNEX H 
[Table 1, SI No. (ix)] 
DETERMINATION OF RESISTIVITY OF AQUEOUS EXTRACT 


H-0 GENERAL 


H-0.1 The resistivity (inverse of conductivity) of the 
aqueous extract is determined to know the ionic 
components, if present in the titanium dioxide. The 
titanium dioxide pigment used in surface coating has 
applications like electrostatic spraying and 
electrodeposition wherein the resistivity is of prime 
importance. 


H-1 REAGENTS 


H-1.1 Water — specific resistivity not less 
2 500 © m or specific conductivity below 4 uS/cm, 
respectively 


H-1.2 Ethanol — specific resistivity preferable not 
less than 2 500 Q m or specific conductivity below 
4 uS/cm, respectively 


H-1.3 Conductivity Calibration Solution — for 
example, potassium chloride 


H-2 APPARATUS 


H-2.1 Cylinder — approximately 35 mm wide by 
125 mm high, or other container suitable for use 
with the conductivity cell 


H-2.2 Digital Conductivity Meter — 
with temperature measurement and __its 
compensation. 


H-2.3 Conductivity Cell — having a cell constant 
K of approximately 1.0 


H-3 PREPARATION OF THE CONDUCTIVITY 
METER 


The conductivity meter and the conductivity cell are 
calibrated using a suitable conductivity calibration 
solution. In case of insufficient congruence of 
equipment display and calibration record, the 
measuring equipment shall be adjusted by correcting 


the cell constant K. 
H-4 PROCEDURE 


An aqueous extract of a pigment suspension shall be 
prepared before performing the conductivity 
measurement. The water-wettability of the pigment 
shall be tested beforehand. In case of low 
wettability, the pigment shall be wetted using as 
much ethanol as necessary to obtain a soft paste. 
This paste is subsequently transferred into a 
suspension by adding water. The pigment 
concentration of the suspension shall be adjusted in 
the range of 5 percent to 10 percent (mass fraction). 


For the extraction, the suspension shall be heated up 
at 60 °C for at least 30 min. For homogenization, the 
suspension shall be stirred or shaken continuously. 
Loss of mass during the warm extraction shall be 
adjusted by adding water to keep the pigment 
concentration at a constant level. Filter the 
suspension after tempering through a fine textured 
filter paper. Separation of solid content may also be 
done by a centrifuge using clean test-glasses. In this 
case, the overlaying liquid is to be filtered through a 
filter paper by decanting. 


For performing the measurement, fill the obtained 
filtrate into the cylinder and place the conductivity 
cell in it. Move the cell slowly up and down to 
remove all air bubbles. The temperature of 
determination should be 27 °C. The measuring cell 
shall be adjusted upright in the middle of the 
cylinder, the measuring opening (vent) around 
10 mm below the surface of the liquid. 
Subsequently, the measurement can be started. 


The result of the measurement is reported as electric 
resistivity in ohm centimeters (Q cm) or as specific 
electric conductivity in microsiemens per 
centimeter (uS/cm), respectively, or in a unit of 
measurement derived from those. 


IS 9788 : 2023 


ANNEX J 
[Table 1, SI No. (x)] 
DETERMINATION OF WATER DEMAND 


J-0 GENERAL 


The water demand test is carried out to know the 
surface area in general and the type of surface 
treatments. It also reveals the particle size and the 
extent of grinding, particularly for rutile of R3 
grade. It facilitates formulation of mill base 
composition. 


J-1 MATERIALS REQUIRED 
J-1.1 Stainless Steel Cup 

J-1.2 Stainless Steel Spatula 
J-1.3 Burette — 0.1 ml graduation 


J-1.4 Sodium Hexametaphosphate — 5 percent 
solution 


J-2 PROCEDURE 


Take about 50 g of titanium dioxide accurately 
weighed in the steel cup and add 0.4 percent 


equivalent on mass basis of pigment, sodium 
hexametaphosphate solution. Add from the burette 
drop by drop distilled water to the powder and mix 
the powder well. After the paste is formed add water 
very carefully and slowly till the flow point is 
achieved. Note the reading on the burette. Calculate 
the total water by adding the burette reading and 
volume in ml of sodium hexametaphosphate 
solution. 


J-3 CALCULATION 


Express the result as ml of water required for 100 g 
of pigment. 


NOTE — Sodium hexametaphosphate is used so that the 
aggregate and agglomerates are broken down and individual 
particles are wetted. 


IS 9788 : 2023 


ANNEX K 
[Table 1, SI No. (xi)] 
SETTLING TEST 


K-0 GENERAL 


Settling tests for air drying and stoving paints are 
prescribed. 


K-1 OUTLINES OF THE METHOD 


Test for settling properties of an drying and stoving 
paints prepared with known amount of titanium 
dioxide pigment and alkyd resin of specified oil 
length is conducted and observations recorded. 


K-2 TEST ON AIR DRYING PAINT 


K-2.1 Formulation of Paint 


Prepare an air-drying paint with drying/semi-drying 
oil alkyd having 60 percent to 62 percent oil length, 
24 percent to 26 percent titanium dioxide and 
60 percent solids in petroleum hydrocarbon solvent. 
The pigment to binder ratio shall be 1 : 1.3. Disperse 
all these ingredients in a ball or sand mill for 
Hegman gauge fineness of 0 mil. The viscosity of 
this paint shall be 100 s to 120 s at 30 °C in IS cup 
No. 4. 


K-2.2 Procedure 


Thin to 30 s viscosity at 30 °C in IS cup no. | with 
petroleum hydrocarbon solvent, low aromatic 
(see IS 1745). Fill it in a 500 ml container to within 
1 cm of the top. Close the container and keep for 
72 h at room temperature. 


K-2.3 Observation 


Open the container after 72 h and observe the 
condition of the material. The requirement of this 
test shall be taken to be satisfied if there is no 
settling, sedimentation or separation of the pigment. 


K-3 TEST ON STOVING PAINT 
K-3.1 Formulation of the Paint 


Prepare a stoving paint with coconut oil alkyd 
having 40 percent oil length, 34 percent titanium 
dioxide content and 60 percent solids in xylene. The 
pigment to binder ratio shall be 1: 2 and alkyd to 
melamine formaldehyde ratio 3.5 : 1. Disperse the 
ingredients in ball or sand mill for Hegman gauge 
fineness of O mil. The viscosity of this paint shall 
be 60 s in IS cup No. 4 at 30 °C. 


K-3.2 Procedure 


Thin to 18 s to 20 s viscosity at 30 °C in IS cup No. 
4 with xylene and butanol in ratio of 9.1. Fill it in a 
500 ml container to within 1 cm of the top. Close 
the container and keep it for 72 h at room 
temperature. 


K-3.3 Observation 


Open the container after 72 h and observe the 
condition of the material. The requirement of this 
test shall be taken to be satisfied if there is no 
settling, sedimentation or separation of the pigment. 


IS 9788 : 2023

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
